title: Why you wake at 3am
summary: Deborah explains the cortisol and blood-sugar rhythm behind early waking, and three gentle evening habits to try.

title: Hot flashes are a hypothalamus story
summary: Your body's thermostat lives in the hypothalamus. Here's what changes in midlife and what tends to help.
body: Hot flashes can feel like they come from nowhere, but they start in a very specific place: the hypothalamus, the part of the brain that keeps your temperature steady.
As estrogen shifts, the hypothalamus can become more sensitive to small changes, and it tries to cool you down when you don't need it.
Steady sleep, regular meals and fewer evening triggers give it a calmer environment to work in. Track what you notice and bring it to your provider.

title: The Five Pillars, in five minutes
summary: A short lesson on the foundations Deborah returns to in every consultation.
body: Sleep, nourishment, movement, stress and connection — the Five Pillars are where Deborah starts with everyone.
None of them needs to be perfect. Pick the one that feels easiest and build from there for two weeks before adding another.

title: Thyroid tests: beyond TSH
summary: What a full thyroid panel includes and how to ask your provider about it.

title: Reading your lab report without panic
summary: Reference ranges, units and why one number never tells the whole story.
body: Lab reports are written for clinicians, so they can look alarming. A value flagged high or low is a starting point for a conversation, not a diagnosis.
Look at the date, the units and the reference range. Then write down how you've been feeling around that time — your provider needs both.

title: First periods: what's typical in the early years
summary: For parents and teens: why cycles take time to settle, and when it's worth asking a provider.
body: In the first couple of years, cycles are often irregular. The hypothalamus is still learning the rhythm.
Very heavy bleeding, cycles more than three months apart, or pain that keeps her from school are good reasons to check in with a provider.

title: Sleep habits for growing bodies
summary: A short talk for teens on why a steady bedtime matters more than you'd think.

title: Stress and your cycle
summary: How stress signals reach your hormones, and small ways to soften them.
body: Stress hormones and reproductive hormones share the same command centre. When stress runs high for weeks, cycles and sleep often change too.
A ten-minute walk, a regular wind-down, and saying no to one thing a week are all real interventions.
